title: Think-Capture: Active 3D Geometry Acquisition for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

problem.summary: Question: When you take the photo in Figure 2, where is the round mirror located relative to you? 1 Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D recognition but often fail to maintain consistent 3D relations across sparse viewpoints, leading to spatial hallucinations under occlusion and perspective changes.
statements: Question: When you take the photo in Figure 2, where is the round mirror located relative to you? 1 Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D recognition but often fail to maintain consistent 3D relations across sparse viewpoints, leading to spatial hallucinations under occlusion and perspective changes.
Existing methods commonly fuse all frames with dense geometry, incurring substantial computation and context overhead while encouraging blind reliance on imperfect estimators.
We present Think-Capture, a query-conditioned framework that first identifies task-critical objects and then acquires their geometry on demand.

limitations.summary: Future work will extend the interface to uncertainty-calibrated, temporally persistent geometry, enabling query-conditioned state refresh within the same hierarchical perception-and-control architecture.
items: Future work will extend the interface to uncertainty-calibrated, temporally persistent geometry, enabling query-conditioned state refresh within the same hierarchical perception-and-control architecture.

Think-Capture has three main limitations: • Foundation-model errors: Although hierarchical GRPO and the empty-return fallback improve tolerance, severe π 3 reconstruction or SAM3 segmentation failures can still propagate to the answer. • Symbolic information loss: Axis-aligned boxes and discrete relations omit fine shape, object orientation, and contact geometry needed for dexterous manipulation.

When Stage 2 predicts the final answer without intermediate chain-of-thought tokens, end-to-end latency falls by more than 40% while MindCube-Tiny accuracy remains 53.2% (versus 54.4% with full reasoning).
